sections.interpretation: The first owned Membership that is not a FeatureMembership determines the common instantiatedType operation. A non-Type first member produces null. The derived property follows the operation, and a separate validation constraint requires a non-null instantiated Type.

InvocationExpression specializes its instantiated Type. The Type must be a Behavior or a Feature typed by one Behavior. Result, parameter, default-value and ownership validations remain separate requirements.

The main implied-relationship row admits FeatureTyping, Subsetting and Specialization for Invocation target specialization, and places Constructor target specialization on its result. The accompanying Note 3 says Subclassification for a Classifier target, which conflicts with a Feature source and the Ecore Subclassification endpoint contract; this inconsistency is recorded below.

agreement: Common non-null first-member selection, rejection of a first non-Type, FeatureMembership exclusion and Invocation versus Constructor effect placement agree in the bounded observations. Physical relation-kind observations agree with Pilot; the normative table-note conflict is not counted as resolved.

The conflicting Note 3 interpretation remains explicit and cannot establish full normative qualification.
